issue: #390-A / #390-B — the parallel wave path wrote no run log and skipped post-apply verification

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: The first version of this test suite proved the fix worked — REFUTED: all four passed against fully-reverted code, because one-resource fixtures never reach the wave path (machine.rs:183 requires >1 change). Rewritten with two-resource fixtures and a guard-the-guard test.

This branch broke cli::tests_build_image::cmd_build_far_produces_valid_archive — REFUTED: it passes in isolation on this branch AND main, has no wave/parallel reference, and a second full run was clean at 13404/0. A parallelism flake.
quorum.divergence: the probe lane initially reported the fix verified; the falsification step contradicted it outright and forced the fixture rewrite. That disagreement is the most valuable output of this quorum.

systems: Kubernetes — admission control runs per object regardless of how many are applied concurrently
Terraform — the -parallelism graph still performs the same post-apply read on every node
Ansible — the `free` strategy varies task ORDER across hosts, never which checks run
systemd — unit verification is per unit, independent of startup concurrency
crux.verdict: no surveyed system varies its verification by scheduler. forjar did, silently, and that is the defect rather than a performance trade-off.

agy_teamwork.verdict: the 1.24.0 review flagged #390-B as HIGHER SEVERITY THAN #390 ITSELF and warned the two halves must land together
unique_findings: capture without update_run_meta leaves `forjar logs --failures` blind, because summary.failed is only incremented by RunMeta::record_resource — recorded as a known limit rather than silently omitted

pmat.quality_gate: new suite absent from the vacuous list; clippy -D warnings 0 errors
